name: Snow
_turns: How many turns a game lasts (the arena doc); the turn track at the table's end has a slot for each.
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. Each character is defined in the legend. From a photo of the user's drawn board (mapstomake/icemap.jpg, taken from player 2's side: turned 180 degrees and perspective-straightened; the board looks the same turned round, only the spawns swap), 18 by 18: high ground round each player's spawns (one level up, its edges sloping down like Yaksha's), low ground through the middle and in the other two corners with the flags, two zigzags of water in the basin, and ice on the high ground that slides a Pokemon off it the way its arrows point.
_legend: level = height step (0 = the low ground); tiles interact only within 1 level. surface picks the look from the palette. slant = the high ground slopes down to lower tiles over this many world units inside the tile (60 degrees, as on Yaksha). sink = the water sits this much lower (a look only). marker = something on the tile (painted, or a 3D piece with piece: true). R/L/U/D/d/u = ice sliding right / left / up / down / down-right / up-left (an arrow painted the way it slides, never turned).
_tile: Built at the usual --tile 3.24875 (the user chose it over smaller tiles): 18 tiles = 58.48 across, so the table stretches front to back for this map (Global.lua setTableDepth: the trims keep their width, the picture covers the board's depth, the team stands move back a tile).
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_table: Image for the table around the board (placeholder until the arena gets its own).
_textures: Placeholders from tools/draw_placeholders.py: fresh snow on the high ground, trampled snow with frozen earth on the low ground, glassy ice, cold water with floating ice, snowy rock round the board's edge.
